transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Martinez (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (Aurora Head of Product), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Dir Eng), Sofia Reyes (Aurora DS), Carlos Vega (Aurora Security)

Summary:
Quick run-through of pilot results, tuning adjustments from last week, alignment on business case and success criteria, confirm next steps for exec review and procurement path.

Topics:
- Performance (latency, throughput)
- Cost and cost model adjustments
- Quality/regression checks (false positives in rerank)
- Security and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)
- Next steps and exec review cadence

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're on for 45, I'll kick off real quick. Maya, Liam, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Yeah, thanks Jamie. We wanna make sure we close the loop on the performance numbers from the end-to-end suite.
[00:17] Ravi Patel: Quick context, last week we pushed updated batching and KV cache settings, plus a small quantized variant for the ranking model. We ran the baseline and the tuned config across the prod-ish traces you shared.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: So what did we see? The last emailed sheet showed p50 around 160ms and p95 closer to 420ms which is... higher than we hoped.
[00:40] Ravi Patel: Right. The initial runs used hosted instances with conservative batching. With the dedicated config we tested yesterday, p50 moves to ~140ms and p95 to about 260-290ms on the same workload. There's a caveat - the 95th is sensitive to long-context requests and some outlier heavy prompts.
[00:55] Sofia Reyes: I noticed the reranker had some false positives, like promotion content being ranked higher than intended. Did you narrow that down?
[01:03] Ravi Patel: Yeah that's a quality tuning issue, mostly prompt/template and temperature. We pushed a rerank threshold change and adjusted the prompt tokens, that cut the false positive rate by approx 18% in our test set. 
[01:16] Maya Thompson: Ok good. From a business case perspective we need to show cost per 1M tokens and also the tail latency for our checkout flow - customers are sensitive to anything above 300ms.
[01:27] Jamie Chen: Understood. We updated the cost model - two scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go and dedicated reserved capacity. I'll share the spreadsheet after the call. For your numbers, with the tuned dedicated config we estimate ~35% cost reduction vs hosted for your throughput ranges.
[01:42] Liam O'Connor: Is that factoring in KV cache hit rate? Our traces had a pretty high prefix reuse so cache should help.
[01:48] Ravi Patel: Yes, the model assumes a 42% KV cache hit for session reuse based on your sample traces. If your cache hit goes above 60% the unit cost drops further.
[01:55] Carlos Vega: From security side, we need SOC2 scope, encryption in transit and at rest, plus KMS integration. Any issues with HSM-backed keys?
[02:05] Noah Martinez: Redwood supports KMS and HSM for Private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations and have SOC2 Type II in our compliance pack. We'll send the security pack link.
[02:15] Carlos Vega: Perfect, please share certs and the audit cadence. Also curious about data retention and how logs are masked.
[02:23] Jamie Chen: We'll include the retention settings and the masking docs. For RBAC and audit logs, those are available in Redwood Private and Dedicated consoles.
[02:30] Maya Thompson: Great. On the pilot success criteria - we shared a draft: p95 < 300ms for checkout flows, average relevance score >= 0.72 on the test set, and TCO within 20% of our current microservices cost baseline. Anything else we should add?
[02:45] Sofia Reyes: Also include error rate targets (5xx < 0.1%) and an uptime window during peak hours.
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: Plus a note on model explainability - we need a short audit trail for ranked decisions for legal.
[02:58] Jamie Chen: We'll add those. Sofia, can you finalize the success criteria doc and share by Thursday?
[03:05] Sofia Reyes: Yep I can get that done, aim for 2026-03-04.
[03:10] Ravi Patel: For the dedicated run, I collected traces and we've uploaded them to the shared folder - there are also latency histograms and KV cache hit heatmaps. We saw the biggest wins on short-turn queries with high prefix reuse.
[03:22] Liam O'Connor: Could you also run a 95th percentile run with simulated checkout traffic? The synthetic traces we used earlier might not capture concurrency spikes.
[03:30] Ravi Patel: Yes, plan to run that overnight and send logs. We'll also include full trace spans so your infra team can correlate.
[03:37] Carlos Vega: On procurement path, we likely need a one-page security appendix and the SOW. What's typical lead time to start Dedicated if we sign?
[03:47] Jamie Chen: For Dedicated we usually have a 4-6 week provisioning timeline depending on capacity and regions; Private (VPC) adds another 2-3 weeks for networking and certs. We can accelerate with upfront commitments.
[03:58] Maya Thompson: That timeline's acceptable if we align exec decision next week. We need clear cost + risk for the exec deck.
[04:06] Noah Martinez: We'll help prep an exec summary; Jamie and I can provide a 1-pager and a short demo video of the end-to-end checkout flow.
[04:12] Jamie Chen: Action items recap - I'll send the updated cost model and pilot summary; Ravi will run dedicated p95 tests and share results; Sofia finalizes success criteria; Carlos shares KMS/HSM procurement constraints.
[04:24] Sofia Reyes: One question - the ranked outputs, can we pin model versions? We need stable reproducibility for audits.
[04:30] Ravi Patel: Yes you can pin model versions in Redwood and we support versioned rollouts, canary, and A/B experiments. We'll document the rollout policy and rollback steps.
[04:39] Liam O'Connor: Any surprises on integration work? We estimate 2 sprint of infra and one sprint of model tuning.
[04:46] Jamie Chen: That matches other customers; we'll attach a sample integration checklist.
[04:50] Maya Thompson: Okay we're good. Let's schedule the exec review for week of the 9th. Can you send calendar invites?
[04:55] Jamie Chen: Yes, we'll propose slots after this call.
[04:58] Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone.
[05:00] Jamie Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the items.

Notes: Transcription has minor errors (names sometimes misattributed), some timestamps approximate. References: shared folder (link: //redwood.share/aurora/pilot-results), security pack (link: //redwood.docs/security-pack.pdf), cost-model sheet (link: //redwood.sheets/aurora-cost-model).

End of transcript.
